summary: Mongolghuraghuri is a Mars terrain mapping and intelligent route planning platform developed to support future planetary exploration. It addresses the challenge of navigating unfamiliar Martian landscapes, where the shortest path may cross steep slopes or difficult terrain. The platform combines NASA's Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA) global elevation data with a higher resolution, 20 meter Jezero Crater CTX Digital Terrain Model to create a hierarchical route planning system. It first generates a broad route corridor across Mars, then refines regional sections using available higher resolution terrain data and slope based analysis. Users can explore interactive map layers, view scientific interest locations, generate terrain aware routes, and examine elevation profiles to better understand the landscape along a journey. By making Martian terrain and route alternatives easier to analyze, Mongolghuraghuri aims to help researchers and future exploration teams make more informed decisions when planning surface traverses.
details:
Project Details – Mongolghuraghuri

Mongolghuraghuri is a Mars terrain mapping and hierarchical route-planning platform designed to support researchers and future planetary exploration missions in understanding and navigating the Martian surface.

How It Works

The platform combines global and regional elevation datasets to plan routes at different levels of detail. It uses NASA's Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA) data to understand large scale Martian topography and generate a broad route corridor across the planet. Where higher resolution terrain data is available, such as the 20 meter CTX Digital Terrain Model covering Jezero Crater, the system refines regional route sections using elevation and slope analysis.

Our routing engine uses an A* pathfinding algorithm with terrain based costs to find alternative paths rather than simply connecting two locations with a straight line. It can retry regional route calculations with adjusted slope thresholds when an initial attempt cannot find a path. If regional refinement fails, it can retain the corresponding section of the broader route corridor and identify it as a fallback.

Users can explore the interactive Mars map, switch between available map layers, view scientific interest locations, select start and destination coordinates, generate routes, and examine route information and elevation profiles.

Benefits and Intended Impact

  • Helps users understand how Martian terrain affects possible travel routes.
  • Provides a way to explore routes across large distances while refining them in areas with higher resolution data.
  • Makes elevation changes, route distance, and regional refinement results easier to inspect.
  • Supports research, mission planning studies, and educational exploration of Mars.
  • Provides a foundation that can be expanded as additional high resolution terrain datasets become available.

Our long term goal is to help researchers and future exploration teams make better informed decisions about traversing unfamiliar planetary landscapes.

Technology and Tools

Backend:

  • Python
  • FastAPI
  • Rasterio for raster elevation data access
  • NumPy for terrain calculations
  • PyProj for coordinate transformations
  • A* pathfinding for route generation

Frontend:

  • Next.js
  • React
  • TypeScript
  • React-Leaflet and Leaflet for interactive planetary mapping

Scientific Data:

  • NASA MOLA global elevation data
  • USGS-produced 20 meter Jezero CTX Digital Terrain Model derived from NASA Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter Context Camera data

Creativity and Innovation

The key creative aspect of Mongolghuraghuri is its hierarchical routing approach. Instead of relying entirely on one dataset or attempting to calculate a detailed route across the entire planet at once, it first creates a broad global route corridor and then refines individual sections using regional terrain data where available.

This allows the platform to combine planetary scale planning with more detailed local analysis through a shared routing architecture. Its adaptive slope retries and identifiable fallback sections also make the route planning process more flexible and transparent.

Factors Considered During Development

Our team considered:

  • Terrain difficulty: Elevation and slope influence route selection.
  • Dataset resolution: Global and regional datasets provide different levels of terrain detail.
  • Data coverage: Higher resolution datasets are not available everywhere, so the system must adapt to their coverage.
  • Coordinate accuracy: Mars specific coordinate reference systems and transformations are essential for correctly positioning terrain and routes.
  • Performance: Large planetary raster datasets require efficient, region based processing rather than loading entire datasets into memory.
  • Reliability: The system identifies unsuccessful regional refinements and uses broader route geometry as a fallback where necessary.
  • Transparency: Route status, refinement information, and elevation profiles help users understand how a route was generated.

Mongolghuraghuri is a research and route planning prototype, not a certified astronaut safety system. Its results depend on the resolution, accuracy and coverage of the available terrain datasets.
